containment.note: An array entry is a `type` (grpent member), and `type` is a `/` type-choice, so a choice may be an element directly. RFC8610 §3.4, §2.2.2; ABNF type2 array -> grpent -> type (type-choice).
`~name` is a type2, valid wherever a type is; as an array element it inlines the unwrapped type's content. RFC8610 §3.4, §3.7; ABNF grpent -> type -> type2 unwrap.

An unnamed INLINE map as an array element. Unsupported: the example has no nominal record name, so cddl-codegen rejects it gracefully; the element-slot `; @name` door can mint a heterogeneous record, while other contexts still require a named rule. Distinct from the anonymous-ARRAY class, which is a separate site keyed on the bracket. RFC8610 §3.4, §3.5.
An array is a type2, valid as an array element (array of arrays). RFC8610 §3.4; ABNF grpent -> type -> type2 array.
A parenthesized inline group is itself a grpent, so a sub-group may appear directly among an array's entries (group-in-group). RFC8610 §2.2; ABNF grpent / inline-group.
A group entry may be a groupname reference, splicing that named group's entries into the array. RFC8610 §2.2.1; ABNF grpent / groupname.

A numeric literal as a fixed array-element value (`[v: 5]`) — supported as a member; the top-level `version = 5` type is not. The literal is a decimal UINT, so its negative sibling is a separate cell: `contain.array-element.value.number.nint`. RFC8610 §2.1, §3.4.

A NEGATIVE numeric literal as a fixed array-element value (`[v: -1]`) — the sign variation of `contain.array-element.value.number`, whose literal is the uint `5`. The kinds are not interchangeable: a fixed nint encodes on CBOR major 1 rather than major 0 and needs its own mismatch rendering, which is why the cell was held back until `Key::Nint` existed to name the AUTHORED value (`-1`) instead of the `-1-N` wire form a uint-only key would have printed. Member position, not arm position: the constant is verified on deserialize and stored nowhere, so a wrong constant is an enforceable `FixedValueMismatch` on this member rather than an arm-selection miss — the reason this cell classifies as enforcement-bearing (`query_q4_directional.ts`) while its arm-position relatives do not. RFC8610 §2.1, §3.4.
A text literal as a fixed array-element value (`[v: "x"]`) — supported as a member; the top-level `marker = "x"` type is not. RFC8610 §2.1, §3.4.
The prelude constant `true` as a fixed array-element member value (`[v: true]`) — supported as a member; the top-level `foo = true` type is not. RFC8610 §2.1, §3.4.
The prelude constant `null` as a fixed array-element member value (`[v: null]`) — distinct from the choice-member nullable pattern. RFC8610 §2.1, §3.4.
A literal value as a member type (`[w: uint, v: 5]`) — the inline fixed-value path, distinct from the nominal standalone `answer = 42` singleton. RFC8610 §2.1, §3.4.
A tag wrapping a fixed null member value (`[v: #6.1(null)]`) — covers the member-position wrapped fixed-value arm, including preserve-encoding emission. RFC8610 §3.4, §3.6.
A tag wrapping a fixed bool member value (`[v: #6.11(true)]`) — covers the member-position wrapped fixed-value arm with a non-null prelude constant. RFC8610 §3.4, §3.6.

The prelude constant `false` as a fixed array-element member value (`[v: false, x: uint]`) — the third of the three fixed prelude constants in this role, beside `contain.array-element.prelude.true` and `.null`, and the array-representation twin of `contain.map-value.prelude.false`. RFC8610 §2.1, §3.4.

The prelude constant `undefined` as a fixed array-element member value (`[v: undefined, x: uint]`) — the fourth fixed prelude constant in this role, completing the sweep beside `contain.array-element.prelude.true` / `.null` / `.false`. Its map-representation twin is `contain.map-value.prelude.undefined`. RFC8610 §2.1, §3.4.

A byte-string literal as a fixed array-element member value (`[v: h'0102', x: uint]`) — the third literal LEXEME kind in this role, beside `contain.array-element.value.number` and `.text`; its map-representation twin is `contain.map-value.value.bytes`. RFC8610 §2.1 (bytes value), §3.4; ABNF grpent -> type -> type2 value -> bytes.

A BARE (unkeyed) literal as an array entry in exactly-once placement (`[5, x: uint]`) — no memberkey, so the grpent is a bare `type` that happens to be a value. The exactly-once side of the fixed-value cardinality boundary; its count-permitting siblings are `contain.occurrence-target.type2.value.zero_array` / `.optional_array` / `.plus_array` (`[* 5]`, `[? 5]`, `[+ 5]`). Distinct from `contain.array-element.type2.value`, which carries a memberkey (`[w: uint, v: 5]`) — keying is the varying axis between the two. RFC8610 §2.1, §3.4; ABNF grpent = type (no memberkey) -> type2 value.

A FLOAT numeric literal as a fixed array-element value (`[v: 1.5]`) — the third KIND of `contain.array-element.value.number`, whose literal is the uint `5`, beside the nint `contain.array-element.value.number.nint`. The kinds are not interchangeable: a fixed float encodes on CBOR major 7 as a float head (`f9`/`fa`/`fb`), so the member reads `raw.float()?` rather than an integer reader, verifies the constant with an exact `!=` compare (`1.5` is `3/2`, exactly representable, so the compare is well-defined) and reports a wrong value as `FixedValueMismatch` with `Key::Float`, and the serialize side writes `write_float(serializer, 1.5)` — the shortest lossless head for the value. Member position, not arm position: the constant is verified on deserialize and stored nowhere, which is why this cell classifies as enforcement-bearing (`query_q4_directional.ts`) while its arm-position relatives do not. The DECIMAL lexeme is what this cell varies; its hexfloat spelling of the same value class is the feature row `value.number.hexfloat` (`[v: 0x1.8p+1]`). Optional (`? f: 2.5`) fixed floats are `tests/corpus/optional_fixed_float.cddl`. RFC8610 §2.1, §3.4.

A byte string constrained via .cbor to encode an INLINE map (controller parenthesized). Unsupported: an inline map in a position requiring a TYPE is not a table, and there is no anonymous representation for it — cddl-codegen rejects it gracefully and names the supported spelling (hoist it to its own rule and reference it). Distinct from the anonymous-ARRAY class, which is a separate site keyed on the bracket. RFC8610 §3.8.4, §3.5.

A byte string constrained to encode a tagged item: `bytes .cbor (#6.10(uint))`. RFC8610 §3.8.4, §3.6; ABNF ctlop controller type2 tagged-data. (uint payload, not int: a bare `int` inside emits the un-emitted Int wrapper and fails the compile-gate — orthogonal to tag-in-cbor.)

The .cbor controller is a type2, so a `/` choice must be parenthesized — `bytes .cbor (int / tstr)`; bare, the `/` would bind at the enclosing type level. RFC8610 §3.8.4, §2.2.2; ABNF type1 ctlop (type2 controller).

containment.example: t = {a: int, c: uint} / {b: tstr, d: uint}
containment.note: An unnamed INLINE map as a `/` choice alternative. Unsupported: the example has no nominal record name, so cddl-codegen rejects it gracefully; a type2 `; @name` can mint the heterogeneous record where that comment slot belongs to the arm, while other contexts require named structs. Distinct from the anonymous-ARRAY class, which is a separate site keyed on the bracket. RFC8610 §2.2.2, §3.5.
An array as a type-choice alternative: `[int] / [tstr]`. RFC8610 §2.2.2, §3.4; ABNF type-choice / type2 array.
Tagged types as choice alternatives (tag-discriminated union): `#6.10(int) / #6.11(tstr)`. RFC8610 §2.2.2, §3.6; ABNF type-choice / type2 tagged-data.

The transparent tag-set idiom: a spec-legal two-arm choice whose arms are the SAME collection but for exactly ONE Tagged op (`#6.258([* uint]) / [* uint]`). cddl-codegen recognizes arms equal-but-for-one-tag — occurrence bounds INCLUDED in the equality — and collapses to ONE transparent optionally-tagged collection alias (`pub type T = Vec<u64>`, IR tag_optional) instead of a two-variant enum: the arm distinction carries no type-level information, so the enum was the accident (doc: current_capacities § 'Transparent tag-set idiom'). Being a transparent alias, it mints no standalone surface — the probe embeds via the synthetic holder, itself a collapse signal. The verdict pins the collapse AND that BOTH wire arms decode: the default encoder serializes tagged, so the UNTAGGED arm is a direction our own output never emits — the foreign untagged vectors (bare-array head, CBOR major 4) are the independent decode evidence, alongside tagged instances (tag-258 head `d9 0102`, major 6). The vendor sibling `dsl.duplicates.reject` pins the reject-flavored idiom; this cell pins the bare/default-preserve collapse. RFC8610 §2.2.2, §3.6; ABNF type-choice / type2 tagged-data.

The one-arm-tagged near miss (`#6.258([+ uint]) / [* uint]`): mismatched occurrence bounds mean the tagged arm (>=1) and untagged arm (empty-allowed) are DIFFERENT logical values, so the equal-but-for-one-tag collapse condition fails and today's two-variant type-choice enum is RETAINED (a tagged `NonEmptyVec<u64>` variant, an untagged `Vec<u64>` variant). This completes the enum-side pinning the both-tagged sibling `contain.choice-member.type2.tag` (`#6.10(int) / #6.11(tstr)`) began, covering the one-arm-tagged case where collapse could plausibly-but-wrongly fire; the retained enum still round-trips both arms standalone. Other near misses (different element types, both arms tagged, 3+ arms, non-collection inner) are pinned in-process in `optional_tag_set_tests.rs` and by `tests/corpus/tag_set_near_miss.cddl`. RFC8610 §2.2.2, §3.6; ABNF type-choice / type2 tagged-data.

`null` as a `/` alternative (`tstr / null`) — the canonical nullable pattern (Option<T>). A standalone `x = null` is instead the nominal null singleton; the feature and containment rows deliberately cover their distinct representations. RFC8610 §2.2.2, App. D.

A two-arm fixed/null choice (`t = true / null`) uses the nullable Option lowering, but its fixed arm is a nominal singleton (`Option<FixedBoolTrue>`) rather than an unstorable inline Fixed. Both legal special values decode; a third special value reaches FixedValueMismatch. This is distinct from the three-arm same-major brute-force cell below: two arms select the dedicated nullable lowering. RFC8610 §2.2.2, §2.2.4.

A bare `any` type-choice arm in a NON-LAST position (`a = any / tstr`). Spec-legal — RFC 8610 places no ordering constraint on `/` alternatives — but cddl-codegen REFUSES it gracefully (exit 1) because a bare `any` accepts every CBOR item, making every later arm unreachable dead code; the message says so and names the remedy (`move it last`). This unsupported verdict is PERMANENT BY DECISION, not pending work: a green flip here would be a REGRESSION, not progress (`README.md` § "Gotchas", the permanent-unsupported bullet, which lists this as the first of its three deliberate boundaries). Pinned by `tests/robustness/choice_any_arm.cddl`. Its supported siblings are `contain.choice-member.prelude.any.last` (the same bare arm, last) and `contain.choice-member.type2.tag.any_non_last` (a tagged `any`, non-last) — position and tagging are the two axes that flip this verdict. RFC8610 §2.2.2, App. D (any).

A bare `any` type-choice arm in the LAST position (`a = tstr / any`) — supported, the catch-all spelling the non-last refusal points at. Dispatch path: BRUTE-FORCE try-each-arm. A bare `any` claims every CBOR major type, so no type-match discriminant can separate it from any sibling; the emitted deserialize anchors `raw.position()`, tries each arm in source order and rewinds on failure, reaching the `AnyCbor` arm only after every earlier arm has declined. That forced backtracking is exactly why the arm must be last and why the sibling cell `contain.choice-member.prelude.any.non_last` is a permanent refusal. RFC8610 §2.2.2, App. D (any).

A TAGGED `any` type-choice arm in a NON-LAST position (`a = #6.10(any) / tstr`) — supported in any position, which is the whole point of the cell: the tag head is a discriminant, so `#6.n(any)` is NOT a catch-all even though its payload is. Dispatch path: TYPE-MATCH — the emitted deserialize matches `raw.cbor_type()`, routes major 6 to the tag arm (checking the tag number, `TagMismatch` otherwise) and major 3 to the text arm, with no backtracking anywhere. Contrast its bare siblings `contain.choice-member.prelude.any.{non_last,last}`: the tag is what buys back the position freedom the bare arm loses. NOT pinned by the two bare-arm robustness fixtures — `tests/robustness/choice_any_arm.cddl` (`any / tstr`) and `tests/robustness/choice_last_any_arm.cddl` (`tstr / any`) both spell the BARE arm and mention the tagged form in prose only. The pins that execute THIS spelling are `tagged_any_arm_allowed_in_any_position` (a first-position `#6.5(any) / tstr`, asserting the AnyCbor lowering and that a deserializer is still generated) and the `choice_tagged_any` rule of `tests/any-positions/input.cddl`, which carries it through the whole-program snapshots and the wasm parity axis. RFC8610 §2.2.2, §2.2.4, §3.6, App. D (any).

A three-arm type choice whose two FIXED arms share a CBOR major type (`t = true / null / tstr`): `true` and `null` are both major 7 specials, so the arm discriminant cannot be the wire major. Dispatch path: BRUTE-FORCE try-each-arm — the emitted deserialize anchors `raw.position()`, runs each arm's reader in source order (the `true` arm verifying its constant as `FixedValueMismatch`, the `null` arm as `ExpectedNull`) and rewinds to the anchor after each failure, ending in `NoVariantMatchedWithCauses`. That is a DISTINCT emission site from the type-match dispatch every other fixed-arm cell in this matrix takes (`contain.group-choice-arm.type2.value.map` and its array-rep siblings), which is why the kind axis has to be probed on both: a fixed kind proven on one path certifies nothing about the other. Deliberately three arms — the two-arm `true / null` is not this shape at all: it now uses the nominal fixed/null Option lowering pinned by `contain.choice-member.type2.value.fixed_null`. Executed under the flag that reaches the site by `fixed_special_type_choice_brute` in `tests/preserve-encodings/input.cddl`. RFC8610 §2.2.2, App. D.

Canonical BOOL representative for the source-derived FixedValue-kind closure: `true / tstr` reaches the bare rule-level type-choice naming and execution path, with a disjoint-major sibling. This is one reviewed representative, not every boolean spelling. RFC8610 §2.2.2, App. D.

Canonical BYTES representative for the source-derived FixedValue-kind closure: `h'CAFE' / tstr`. The uppercase hex spelling avoids the rust-cddl lowercase-parser limitation while exercising the byte-vector-derived variant and wire path. One representative only. RFC8610 §2.2.2, §2.2.4.

Canonical FLOAT representative for the source-derived FixedValue-kind closure: `1.5 / tstr` is spec-legal and generates with the canonical fallback variant `Float3FF8000000000000`, its exact IEEE-754 identity, because the legacy display-derived `F1.5` is unspellable. Spellable legacy fixed-value names remain unchanged; `@name` is optional and still wins when authored. One representative only. RFC8610 §2.2.2, §2.2.4.

Canonical NINT representative for the source-derived FixedValue-kind closure: `-1 / null / tstr` is spec-legal and generates with the canonical fallback variant `Nint1`, because the legacy display-derived `U-1` is unspellable; the third arm avoids the two-arm `/ null` collapse. Spellable legacy fixed-value names remain unchanged. One representative only. RFC8610 §2.2.2, §2.2.4.

Canonical NULL representative for the source-derived FixedValue-kind closure: `null / tstr / uint`. Three arms deliberately prevent the dedicated two-arm `/ null` Option collapse, so null remains a fixed choice arm. One representative only. RFC8610 §2.2.2, App. D.

Canonical TEXT representative for the source-derived FixedValue-kind closure: `"x" / uint` keeps the spellable legacy variant `X` and round-trips. Unspellable text-derived names use the canonical UTF-8 fallback instead: `"self"` is `Text73656C66`, while empty, punctuation-only, and digit-led text follow the same kind-prefixed scheme. RFC8610 §2.2.2, §2.2.4.

Canonical UINT representative for the source-derived FixedValue-kind closure: `5 / tstr` mints a spellable fixed-value variant and exercises the disjoint-major type-choice path. One representative only. RFC8610 §2.2.2, §2.2.4.

Canonical UNDEFINED representative for the source-derived FixedValue-kind closure: `undefined / tstr` exercises the fixed special arm beside a disjoint-major sibling. One representative only. RFC8610 §2.2.2, App. D.

containment.example:
foo<a> = [a]
bar = foo<{x: int, y: uint}>
containment.note: An INLINE map bound to a generic parameter. Unsupported: an inline map in a position requiring a TYPE is not a table, and there is no anonymous representation for it — cddl-codegen rejects it gracefully and names the supported spelling (bind a named-type argument). Distinct from the anonymous-ARRAY class, which is a separate site keyed on the bracket. RFC8610 §3.10.

Each generic argument is a `type1`, which excludes the `/` type-choice (a `type`); bare `foo<int / tstr>` is rejected by both oracles. Parenthesize — `foo<(int / tstr)>` — to pass a choice as one argument. RFC8610 §3.10; ABNF genericarg / type1.
Baseline map-representation group-choice arm with a bareword text key. RFC8610 §2.2.2, §3.5.1.

containment.example:
t = { a: st // b: tstr }
st = [x: uint, y: tstr]
containment.note: Map-representation group-choice arm whose bareword-keyed value is a named RECORD type (`a: st`, `st = [x: uint, y: tstr]`) rather than a scalar. The arm collapses to a variant that dispatches on the fixed key `a`, so the record's own array wire header sits one level in and never reaches the arm discriminant — green even when the sibling arm overlaps. RFC8610 §2.2.2, §3.5.1.
Map-representation group-choice arm with a supported fixed uint key. RFC8610 §2.2.2, §3.5.1.
Map-representation group-choice arm with a supported fixed text key. RFC8610 §2.2.2, §3.5.1.

Map-representation group-choice arm with a fixed negative integer key. Key writing/verification is only implemented for uint/text keys, matching the record map path; real nint support should land there before this flips to supported. RFC8610 §2.2.2, §3.5.1.

Map-representation group-choice arm with a fixed float key. Key writing/verification is only implemented for uint/text keys, matching the record map path; real float-key support should land there before this flips to supported. RFC8610 §2.2.2, §3.5.1.

Map-representation group-choice arm with a non-fixed key (`k => v`). Collapsing such an arm into an enum variant has nowhere to store the key and used to silently drop it; supporting this requires real table-arm dispatch. RFC8610 §2.2.2, §3.5.2.

Map-representation group-choice arm whose entry has no member key. A CBOR map arm must write key/value pairs, so a keyless arm has no well-formed wire shape; the Ruby reference rejects it as a map entry without member key while the Rust oracle accepts the grammar. A plain-group arm works because the referenced group owns its keys.

containment.example:
g = { grp // b: tstr }
grp = (a: uint)
containment.note: Map-representation group-choice arm that references a named group; the referenced group owns the map keys. RFC8610 §2.2.1, §2.2.2.

containment.example: t = { a: uint, b: tstr // c: bytes }
containment.note: Map-representation group-choice arm with multiple fields, pinning arm dispatch for a whole grpchoice sequence rather than a single entry. RFC8610 §2.2.1, §2.2.2.
Map-representation group-choice arm with a fixed-value member type, a distinct dispatch/generation surface from fixed keys. RFC8610 §2.1, §2.2.2.
Baseline array-representation group-choice arm: arms are positional entries and carry no map keys. RFC8610 §2.2.2, §3.4.

containment.example:
t = [ a: st // b: tstr ]
st = [x: uint, y: tstr]
containment.note: Array-representation group-choice arm whose member value is a named RECORD type (`a: st`, `st = [x: uint, y: tstr]` with a uint first field) rather than a scalar. A non-embedded record arm serializes NESTED — the outer array header then the record's OWN array header — so the arm's deserialize discriminant must peek the record's Array header, not its first field's uint type; otherwise spec-valid bytes fall through to NoVariantMatched against the overlapping `tstr` sibling. RFC8610 §2.2.2, §3.4.

containment.example:
t = [ a: tg // b: tstr ]
tg = #6.10([x: uint])
containment.note: Array-representation group-choice arm whose member value is a named TAGGED record type (`a: tg`, `tg = #6.10([x: uint])`) — the tag-head variation of the record_array sibling. The arm's deserialize discriminant routes through `RustType::cbor_types`, whose struct-tag branch dispatches on the record's TAG head (CBOR major type 6), not its Array representation: an alternative discriminant that hand-mapped the record's rep (always Array/Map, never Tag) would dispatch tagged-record arms on the WRONG head type and fall through to NoVariantMatched on spec-valid bytes — while staying green through every untagged record-arm gate. This row is what makes that mis-mapping fail loudly. RFC8610 §2.2.2, §2.2.4, §3.4.

containment.example: t = [ a: uint, b: tstr // c: bytes ]
containment.note: Array-representation group-choice arm with multiple entries, pinning arm dispatch for a whole grpchoice sequence. RFC8610 §2.2.1, §2.2.2, §3.4.
Array-representation group-choice arm that references a named group. RFC8610 §2.2.1, §2.2.2, §3.4.
Array-representation group-choice arm containing an inline parenthesized group. RFC8610 §2.2.1, §2.2.2, §3.4.

Array-representation group-choice arm carrying a fixed NEGATIVE integer member value (`[ v: -1 // label: tstr ]`) — the array-rep, nint-kind counterpart of `contain.group-choice-arm.type2.value.map` (`{ a: 0 // b: tstr }`, a fixed uint in the map rep). Dispatch path: TYPE-MATCH — the emitted deserialize reads the array header then matches `raw.cbor_type()`, routing CBOR major 1 (NegativeInteger) to this arm and major 3 (Text) to the sibling; the arm then verifies the constant and stores nothing, reporting a wrong constant as `FixedValueMismatch` with a `Key::Nint` naming the AUTHORED value (`-1`), not the `-1-N` wire form. No backtracking is emitted, so this row measures the type-match site only. RFC8610 §2.1, §2.2.2, §3.4.

Array-representation group-choice arm whose member is a TAG-WRAPPED fixed value (`[ v: #6.11(true) // label: tstr ]`) — the arm-position counterpart of the member-position cells `contain.array-element.type2.tag.fixed_null` / `.fixed_bool`. Dispatch path: TYPE-MATCH, two-level — `raw.cbor_type()` routes CBOR major 6 (Tag) here and major 3 (Text) to the sibling, then a second match on `raw.tag()` admits 11 and rejects anything else as `TagMismatch`, after which the wrapped constant is verified as `FixedValueMismatch` and stored nowhere. The tag head is what makes the arm discriminable, so unlike the bare fixed specials this kind never needs the brute-force path. RFC8610 §2.1, §2.2.2, §2.2.4, §3.4, §3.6.

Array-representation group-choice arm containing an unnamed map type; this example isolates the remaining no-name rejection inside a `//` arm. Its entry-slot `; @name` can mint a heterogeneous record, while a homogeneous inline table still has no record to name. RFC8610 §2.2.2, §3.4, §3.5.

Array-representation group-choice arm carrying a fixed FLOAT member value beside a sibling arm of a DISJOINT CBOR major (`[ v: 1.5 // label: tstr ]`) — the float-kind counterpart of `contain.group-choice-arm.type2.value.nint_array` (a fixed nint) and `contain.group-choice-arm.type2.value.map` (a fixed uint, map rep). Dispatch path: TYPE-MATCH — the emitted deserialize reads the array header then matches `raw.cbor_type()`, routing CBOR major 7 (Special) to this arm and major 3 (Text) to the sibling; the arm then reads `raw.float()?`, verifies the constant with an exact `!=` compare and stores nothing, reporting a wrong constant as `FixedValueMismatch` with `Key::Float`, and falls through to `NoVariantMatched` on any other major. No backtracking is emitted, so this row measures the type-match site only — the same-major sibling arm is `contain.group-choice-arm.type2.value.float_same_major_array`. RFC8610 §2.1, §2.2.2, §3.4.

Array-representation group-choice arm carrying a fixed FLOAT member value beside an arm that SHARES its CBOR major (`[ v: 1.5 // flag: true ]`) — `1.5` and `true` are both major 7, so the wire major cannot be the arm discriminant. Dispatch path: BRUTE-FORCE try-each-arm — the emitted deserialize reads the array header, anchors `raw.position()`, runs each arm's reader in source order (the float arm verifying its constant as `FixedValueMismatch` with `Key::Float`, the bool arm as `FixedValueMismatch` with `Key::Bool`) and rewinds to the anchor after each failure, ending in `NoVariantMatchedWithCauses`. That is a DISTINCT emission site from the type-match dispatch its disjoint-major sibling `contain.group-choice-arm.type2.value.float_array` takes, which is why the float kind is enumerated on both. The group-choice spelling is deliberate: the same pairing as a bare TYPE choice is a different (and currently defective) path — see `cddl-matrix/roadmap.toml` § findings. RFC8610 §2.1, §2.2.2, §3.4, App. D.
A `type1 =>` memberkey admits any type1; an array (type2) is a valid composite key: `{ [int] => tstr }`. RFC8610 §3.5.2; ABNF memberkey / type1 "=>".

A memberkey is a `type1`, which does NOT include the `/` type-choice (a `type`); the bare form `{ int / tstr => bool }` is rejected by both oracles. Parenthesizing — `(int / tstr)` — turns it into a type2 and is then a valid key. RFC8610 §3.5.2; ABNF memberkey / type1 (type1 excludes type-choice).
Single-entry struct map with a fixed uint colon key. RFC8610 §3.5.1.
Multi-entry struct map with a fixed uint colon key plus a sibling, pinning arity-sensitive record routing. RFC8610 §3.5.1.
Single-entry fixed-value arrow key. A literal-key `k => v` is the same wire entry as `k: v`, so it must route to the record path rather than table-detecting a fixed domain.
Multi-entry fixed-value arrow key with a sibling, pinning arrow-key record routing beyond the single-entry case. RFC8610 §3.5.2.

A NON-literal (type-domain) arrow key with NO occurrence marker: `{ tstr => uint }`. RFC8610 §2.1/§3.2 gives it an exact 1..=1 occurrence window, so cddl-codegen emits `BoundedMap<String, u64, 1, 1>` rather than widening it to a loose table. The literal-key `*_arrow_single` cells still route through the record path.
Single-entry struct map with a fixed text colon key. RFC8610 §3.5.1.
Multi-entry struct map with a fixed text colon key plus a sibling. RFC8610 §3.5.1.
Single-entry fixed text arrow key; equivalent wire shape to the colon spelling but a distinct parser/generator route. RFC8610 §3.5.2.
Multi-entry fixed text arrow key with a sibling, pinning arrow-key record routing. RFC8610 §3.5.2.
Single-entry struct map with a fixed negative integer key. Only uint/text fixed keys are implemented on the record path; this should reject gracefully until real nint key support lands.
Multi-entry struct map with a fixed negative integer key plus a supported sibling, matching the hand-pin shape for unsupported record-map keys.
Single-entry fixed negative integer arrow key; it must reject gracefully rather than exposing a fixed-domain table path.
Multi-entry fixed negative integer arrow key with a sibling; unsupported nint fixed keys should reject gracefully on the record path.
Single-entry struct map with a fixed float key. Only uint/text fixed keys are implemented on the record path; this should reject gracefully until real float key support lands.
Multi-entry struct map with a fixed float key plus a supported sibling. Unsupported float fixed keys should reject gracefully, not panic.
Single-entry fixed float arrow key; it must reject gracefully rather than exposing a fixed-domain table path.
Multi-entry fixed float arrow key with a sibling; unsupported float fixed keys should reject gracefully on the record path.
Single-entry fixed bool arrow key. Bool fixed keys are expressible through `true => v`; the colon spelling `true:` is a bareword text key and is intentionally not a bool cell.
Multi-entry fixed bool arrow key with a sibling. Unsupported bool fixed keys should reject gracefully rather than panic.

containment.example: m = { k: int / tstr, j: uint }
containment.note: A member's value is a `type`, which is a `/` type-choice, so the value may be a choice. RFC8610 §3.5.1, §2.2.2; ABNF grpent (memberkey type) -> type-choice. (2-field example by this file's convention, not a workaround: a single-field bareword map is itself supported, pinned by tests/corpus/single_field_map.cddl.)

An INLINE array as a member value. Unsupported: a heterogeneous inline array in a position requiring a TYPE becomes a struct, and a struct needs a name — where no `@name` comment can reach the site there is none to be had, so cddl-codegen rejects it gracefully and names both remedies (an explicit rule, or `; @name`). RFC8610 §3.5.1, §3.4.

A tagged type (#6.n) as a member value. RFC8610 §3.5.1, §3.6; ABNF grpent value -> type2 tagged-data. (2-field example by this file's convention, not a workaround: a single-field bareword map is itself supported, pinned by tests/corpus/single_field_map.cddl.)

The prelude constant `false` as a fixed map-member value (`{ k: false }`) — supported as a member; the top-level `foo = false` type is not. RFC8610 §2.1, §3.5.1. (2-field example by this file's convention, not a workaround: a single-field bareword map is itself supported, pinned by tests/corpus/single_field_map.cddl.)

`~name` (unwrap) as a member value. Unsupported because type2.unwrap is unsupported at all (not a context effect). RFC8610 §3.5.1, §3.7. (2-field example by this file's convention, not a workaround: a single-field bareword map is itself supported, pinned by tests/corpus/single_field_map.cddl.)

The prelude constant `true` as a fixed map-member value (`{ k: true, j: uint }`) — beside the existing `contain.map-value.prelude.false`, and the map-representation twin of `contain.array-element.prelude.true`. RFC8610 §2.1, §3.5.1.

The prelude constant `null` as a fixed map-member value (`{ k: null, j: uint }`) — the map-representation twin of `contain.array-element.prelude.null`, and distinct from the choice-member nullable pattern (`contain.choice-member.prelude.null`), where `null` is an ARM rather than the whole value. RFC8610 §2.1, §3.5.1.

The prelude constant `undefined` as a fixed map-member value (`{ k: undefined, j: uint }`) — completes the four fixed prelude constants in this role beside `contain.map-value.prelude.true` / `.null` / `.false`; its array-representation twin is `contain.array-element.prelude.undefined`. RFC8610 §2.1, §3.5.1.

A tag WRAPPING a fixed null member value (`{ k: #6.1(null), j: uint }`) — the map-representation mirror of the array-element precedent `contain.array-element.type2.tag.fixed_null`, so the wrapped fixed-value arm is enumerated in both representations. Distinct from the plain `contain.map-value.type2.tag` (`#6.10(int)`), whose tag content is a TYPE rather than a literal. RFC8610 §3.5.1, §3.6, §2.1.

A tag WRAPPING a fixed bool member value (`{ k: #6.11(true), j: uint }`) — the map-representation mirror of the array-element precedent `contain.array-element.type2.tag.fixed_bool`, varying the wrapped constant away from `null` beside its `.fixed_null` sibling. RFC8610 §3.5.1, §3.6, §2.1.

A numeric literal LEXEME as a fixed map-member value (`{ k: 5, j: uint }`) — the map-representation twin of `contain.array-element.value.number`. Paired with `contain.map-value.type2.value` exactly as the array file pairs `contain.array-element.value.number` with `contain.array-element.type2.value`: the two shapes key on the literal-lexeme feature and the literal-as-type2 feature respectively. RFC8610 §2.1, §3.5.1.

A text literal as a fixed map-member value (`{ k: "x", j: uint }`) — the map-representation twin of `contain.array-element.value.text`, and the second literal lexeme kind in this role beside `contain.map-value.value.number`. RFC8610 §2.1, §3.5.1.

A byte-string literal as a fixed map-member value (`{ k: h'0102', j: uint }`) — the third literal lexeme kind in this role beside `contain.map-value.value.number` / `.text`, and the map-representation twin of `contain.array-element.value.bytes`. RFC8610 §2.1 (bytes value), §3.5.1; ABNF grpent memberkey type -> type2 value -> bytes.

A literal used as a member TYPE in map-value position (`{ j: uint, k: 5 }`) — the map-representation twin of `contain.array-element.type2.value` (`[w: uint, v: 5]`), and the type2-axis half of the pair whose lexeme-axis half is `contain.map-value.value.number`. The literal follows an ordinary typed member, matching the array precedent's ordering. RFC8610 §2.1, §3.5.1; ABNF grpent memberkey S type -> type2 value.

An occurrence repeating an unnamed INLINE map entry. Unsupported: the example has no nominal record name, so cddl-codegen rejects it gracefully; where the map is the member's whole type, `; @name` can mint that record, otherwise hoist it to its own rule. Distinct from the anonymous-ARRAY class, which is a separate site keyed on the bracket. RFC8610 §3.2, §3.5.
Occurrence over an array entry: `[* [int]]` (a variable-length list of arrays). RFC8610 §3.2, §3.4; ABNF grpent [occur] ... type2 array.
One occurrence applies to a whole parenthesized sub-group, repeating the entire entry tuple: `[* (int, tstr)]`. RFC8610 §3.2, §2.2; ABNF grpent / [occur] inline-group.

A one-or-more occurrence on an inline array group repeats the tuple. The generator should reject rather than silently narrowing the group to exactly once; supporting this requires real Vec-of-synthesized-group support. RFC8610 §3.2, §3.4.
An optional occurrence on an inline array group permits the tuple to be absent. The generator should reject rather than silently narrowing the group to exactly once. RFC8610 §3.2, §3.4.
A bounded occurrence on an inline array group repeats the tuple. The generator should reject rather than silently narrowing the group to exactly once. RFC8610 §3.2, §3.4.
An exactly-once occurrence on an inline array group has exactly the same semantics as flattening the group once, so flattening is sound. RFC8610 §3.2, §3.4.

A zero-permitting occurrence on an inline map group permits the keyed entry to be absent. The generator should reject rather than silently narrowing it to mandatory; supporting this requires real Option-style support for zero-permitting map markers. RFC8610 §3.2, §3.5.
A one-or-more occurrence on an inline map group collapses to mandatory under unique map keys, so flattening to one keyed field is sound. RFC8610 §3.2, §3.5.
A zero-or-more occurrence on a parenthesized table entry remains a table (`BTreeMap`) rather than a zero-permitting struct field. RFC8610 §3.2, §3.5.2.

A zero-permitting occurrence on a unique keyed struct-map field permits the entry to be absent. cddl-codegen normalizes `*` to the same Option-style carrier as `?`; unique keys rule out a second entry. Exactly-zero `*0` / `0*0` is instead a supported forbidden-key constraint, not an optional carrier. RFC8610 §3.2, §3.5.1.

A bounded positive-upper occurrence with lower bound zero on a unique keyed struct-map field permits absence. cddl-codegen normalizes `0*1` (and positive `*n`) to the Option-style optional-field carrier; unique keys rule out a second entry. Exactly-zero `*0` / `0*0` is instead a supported forbidden-key constraint. RFC8610 §3.2, §3.5.1.

An exactly-zero occurrence on a fixed keyed struct-map field forbids that key (`0*0` / `*0`), rather than making it optional. cddl-codegen retains the constraint outside ordinary fields, rejects the key in CBOR/JSON and checked open-map construction, and never exposes it through a rest map. RFC8610 §3.2, §3.5.1.

A zero-permitting occurrence on a unique uint fixed-key record member (`* 1: uint`) permits the entry to be absent. The `1:` and `1 =>` spellings are the same record-path wire entry and cddl-codegen normalizes both to the Option-style carrier; exact-zero is the supported forbidden-key boundary. RFC8610 §3.2, §3.5.1.

A one-or-more occurrence on a NON-literal (type-domain) arrow map entry: `{ + tstr => uint }` requires 1..N entries (RFC8610 §3.2 `+` = one-or-more, §3.5.2 admits a type1 key). Home here because the varying axis is the occurrence MARKER on the arrow entry (its no-occurrence sibling `contain.map-key.memberkey.type1.tstr_arrow_nooccur` lives in map-key.toml because ITS axis was the key spelling). cddl-codegen honors the `+` lower bound as a NonEmptyMap<String, u64> whose single TryFrom door rejects the empty map, so the row's decode-catalog empty-map vector (holder `[0, {}]` = `8200a0`) is a class="constraint" enforcement reject pin (`enforce = yes`); the unbounded upper direction matches the spec. Enumerated with its boundary-violation vector per the 'Intra-alternative variation rows' rule.

An optional occurrence on a type-domain arrow map entry: `{ ? tstr => uint }` permits 0..1 entries (RFC8610 §3.2 `?` = optional, §3.5.2). cddl-codegen represents it as `BoundedMap<String, u64, 0, 1>` and checks every construction/decode boundary; the empty holder-map vector `8200a0` is valid, while a two-entry map is a constraint rejection.

A bounded occurrence on a type-domain arrow map entry: `{ 2*3 tstr => uint }` requires 2..3 entries (RFC8610 §3.2 `n*m`, §3.5.2). cddl-codegen represents it as `BoundedMap<String, u64, 2, 3>` and checks the inclusive window at API, CBOR, JSON, wasm, and component doors.

The loose open struct-map rest row: a final `* K => V` after >=1 fixed key (`{ 1: uint, * uint => any }`). cddl-codegen captures it in an empty-capable `rest` carrier (BTreeMap, preserve OrderedHashMap, or PairMap under `@duplicates preserve`), with flattened JSON, a wasm rest wrapper, and opaque extern projection. This is the `0*`/unbounded case; the sibling `open_struct_plus` and `open_struct_bounded` cells carry their own row-local checked NonEmpty/Bounded carrier rather than changing the enclosing record's count. CBOR and JSON stage loose entries then cross that carrier's one `TryFrom` door. `@ignore` remains loose-only: dropping a restricted row either re-serializes zero against a positive minimum or loses a zero-minimum window's bounded/exact state. RFC8610 §3.2, §3.5.2.

A one-or-more occurrence on an open struct-map rest row (`{ 1: uint, + uint => any }`) is supported as `NonEmptyMap` (or `NonEmptyPairMap` under `@duplicates preserve`). It is an explicit checked-carrier constructor parameter, and CBOR/JSON stage a loose row then call its single `TryFrom`; the public carrier cannot be emptied. WASM crosses the restricted structural wrapper and component despecializes it to a fallible list-of-pairs constructor argument. This is row-local: the declared fixed member does not count. Pinned by `open_struct_map_rest_row_front_end`, `open_table_e2e`, and the component bounds fixture. RFC8610 §3.2, §3.5.2.

A finite row-local window on an open struct-map rest row (`{ 1: uint, 2*3 uint => text }`) is supported as `BoundedMap<u64, String, 2, 3>` (or its `BoundedPairMap` twin). The window counts captured rest entries only. Native construction accepts the complete checked carrier; CBOR/JSON first collect the loose carrier and enter one `TryFrom` door; WASM/component use their checked boundary conversion. Flattened JSON Schema deliberately omits object-wide `minProperties`/`maxProperties` because those would count the fixed member too. RFC8610 §3.2, §3.5.2.

containment.example:
m = { 1: uint, * k => any }
k = uint / text
containment.note: A rest row whose key domain is a NAMED RULE (`m = { 1: uint, * k => any }`, `k = uint / text`) rather than the bare `uint` of `contain.occurrence-target.memberkey.type1.open_struct`. Supported: a nominal `K` takes the seek path — the loop hoists a `raw.position()` anchor, the declared-key match arms rewind to it when they decline, and `K::deserialize` then reads the key itself, so the write and read halves are the SAME `K` codec by construction rather than a peeked head and a separate writer. A union `K` is the interesting nominal shape because each of its arms must leave the declared keys reachable; declared keys peel first and never reach `K::deserialize`. RFC8610 §3.2, §3.5.2; ABNF grpent [occur] ... memberkey type1 '=>'.

A rest row whose key domain is `bytes` (`m = { 1: uint, * bytes => any }`) — supported, capturing into a `BTreeMap<Vec<u8>, _>`. The byte-string domain is the sidecar-bearing member of this family: under `--preserve-encodings` a `bytes` key contributes a `StringEncoding` bound by the key's own deserialize rather than by a peek, which is the concrete reason a rest key's codec has to be symmetric rather than head-peeked. Its JSON face is a pure error surface (a byte string has no member-name image), so the row also marks where the flattened-rest JSON convention stops. RFC8610 §3.2, §3.5.2; ABNF grpent [occur] ... memberkey type1 '=>'.

A rest row whose key domain is `nint` (`m = { 1: uint, * nint => any }`) — supported. The sign axis of the integer key domain: the captured keys land on CBOR major 1 while the map's own declared key `1` sits on major 0, so the row's key dispatch separates them by wire major before any rewind is needed. Named beside the named-rule and `bytes` siblings because the delivered boundary is 'any deserializable non-float, non-null-admitting `K`', and an enumeration that showed only `uint`-shaped domains would understate it. RFC8610 §3.2, §3.5.2; ABNF grpent [occur] ... memberkey type1 '=>'.

The FLOAT boundary of the rest row's key domain (`m = { 1: uint, * float => any }`). Spec-legal (RFC8610 §3.5.2 admits any type1 as a member key), but cddl-codegen REJECTS it gracefully, naming the rule and the reason: floats have no total order, so they cannot key the capture container. The guard is transitive — it walks the domain, so a struct or union with a float ANYWHERE inside it (`k = [x: float64, y: uint]`) is refused on the same message — which is why one cell covers the whole float-containing class rather than one per nesting depth. This is a reject fixture (tests/matrix_reject/), not a decode-catalog row. The same boundary in the TABLE-key position is `contain.map-key.memberkey.type1.float_arrow_single` and its siblings; pinned by `open_struct_map_rest_row_front_end` (robustness_tests.rs). RFC8610 §3.2, §3.5.2; ABNF grpent [occur] ... memberkey type1 '=>'.

containment.example:
m = { 1: uint, * k => any }
k = text / null
containment.note: The NULL-ADMITTING boundary of the rest row's key domain (`m = { 1: uint, * k => any }`, `k = text / null`). Spec-legal, but cddl-codegen REJECTS it gracefully: a `null` key and the `break` that ends an indefinite-length map are both CBOR major-7 specials, so the row's key dispatch cannot tell 'another captured entry keyed null' from 'the map ended' — the refusal names that collision and points at dropping the `null` arm, since an absent entry already means absent. The rejection is about the key domain ADMITTING null, not about it being exactly `null`: the arm is refused wherever it sits in `K`. Distinct from the float boundary next to it (`contain.occurrence-target.memberkey.type1.open_struct_float_key`), whose reason is ordering rather than wire ambiguity — two independent exclusions, hence two cells. Reject fixture (tests/matrix_reject/), not a decode-catalog row; pinned by `open_struct_map_rest_row_front_end` (robustness_tests.rs). RFC8610 §3.2, §3.5.2; ABNF grpent [occur] ... memberkey type1 '=>'.

The loose open table: a named map of exactly TWO non-fixed type-domain arrow rows and no fixed key (`t = { * bstr => uint, * uint => uint }`). The typed (first) row claims one statically-known CBOR major and the catch-all sees the complement; a typed-major key that its own type refuses is a hard error rather than a capture. Each row owns its own `@duplicates`, checked occurrence carrier, and preserve sidecars: `*`/`0*` are loose, `+`/`1*` are NonEmpty, and finite/other bounded windows use BoundedMap or BoundedPairMap. Under preserve the two dynamic sequences share one order vector and canonical form merges them by encoded key bytes. Named rules only: inline, group-choice/plain-group, >2-row, and fixed-key mixtures refuse. Docs: output_format.mdx section 'Open tables (a typed row plus a catch-all)', comment_dsl.mdx section 'Open tables'. RFC8610 §3.2, §3.5.2; ABNF grpent [occur] ... memberkey type1 '=>'.

A one-or-more occurrence on an open table's TYPED row (`t = { + bstr => uint, * uint => uint }`) is its own NonEmpty region: the minimum counts typed entries only. Its `NonEmptyMap`/`NonEmptyPairMap` public field cannot be emptied; native, wasm, WIT, and JSON retain the established `new(first_key, first_value)` ABI, while CBOR stages loose then uses the shared checked door. The catch-all's count is independent. `+`/`1*` are the NonEmpty spelling and `*`/`0*` loose; `?` and other windows are represented by Bounded carriers (the bounded typed sibling below). Pinned by `open_table_front_end` and `tests/open-table-e2e`. RFC8610 §3.2, §3.5.2.

A bounded typed row in an open table (`t = { 2*3 bstr => uint, * uint => uint }`) is supported as a row-local `BoundedMap`/`BoundedPairMap`; catch-all entries neither satisfy nor consume its window. Native construction takes the checked carrier; CBOR/JSON stage loose entries then call `TryFrom`. WASM keeps the typed accessor surface flattened and fallibly converts its loose builder before native construction; component accepts a fallible list-of-pairs. JSON Schema intentionally omits object-wide property counts. RFC8610 §3.2, §3.5.2.

A one-or-more occurrence on the CATCH-ALL row (`t = { * bstr => uint, + uint => uint }`) is supported as an independent `NonEmptyMap`/`NonEmptyPairMap` region. It is an explicit checked-carrier constructor parameter on native, wasm, and component faces; CBOR/JSON stage the loose catch-all then enter `TryFrom`. Typed entries do not count toward this bound. RFC8610 §3.2, §3.5.2.

A bounded catch-all row in an open table (`t = { * bstr => uint, 2*3 uint => uint }`) is supported as a row-local `BoundedMap`/`BoundedPairMap`. Its checked wrapper crosses native/WASM construction and a fallible component list conversion; CBOR and JSON stage only the catch-all entries before the one `TryFrom`. The typed region is excluded from its count, and JSON Schema stays silent rather than claiming an object-wide property bound. RFC8610 §3.2, §3.5.2.

A zero-or-more occurrence on a bare-type entry in a HETEROGENEOUS array is an open-array segment. A final `* t` tail is supported, as is the one safe non-final shape: a leading/middle segment whose immediate fixed suffix is mandatory, exactly one CBOR item, field-codec-free, and CBOR-major-disjoint from `t` (`[uint, * bytes, tstr]`). Each effective boundary head is generator-proven (including mandatory outer framing) or declared by a transparent custom-codec alias with `@custom_wire_major`; an undeclared custom-owned or direct opaque-extern head remains unproven. The decoder obeys RFC 8610 greedy non-backtracking matching: it consumes repeated element majors without rewind and stops at that disjoint suffix. A finite exact `N*N` segment instead stops by count, needs no major discriminator, and stores ordinary/preserve data as `[T; N]` (exact reject remains `BoundedOrderedSet<T, N, N>`); uniquely named finite exact segments may be adjacent. Variable same-major/value-discriminator, variable multiple, and group/group-choice/plain-group forms stay rejected gracefully. `*` captures `Vec<T>`, `+` `NonEmptyVec<T>`, and variable bounded windows `BoundedVec<T, MIN, MAX>`. Under --preserve-encodings each captured segment element re-serializes byte-exactly via a positional per-element sidecar (a self-carried `any` element needs none), and --canonical-form normalizes each element in source position; the loose captured `Vec<T>` renders as an ordinary JSON array field (skip-if-empty on write, default-on-read) and exposes a read-only wasm `rest()` list-wrapper getter. RFC8610 §3.2, §3.4.

A one-or-more occurrence on a bare-type entry in a HETEROGENEOUS array is a restricted open-array segment: it may be final, or a safe middle segment before an immediate mandatory, one-item, field-codec-free, CBOR-major-disjoint suffix. Each effective boundary head is generator-proven (including mandatory outer framing) or declared by a transparent custom-codec alias with `@custom_wire_major`; an undeclared custom-owned or direct opaque-extern head remains unproven. The `+ t` / `1* t` segment captures repeated elements in `NonEmptyVec<T>`. Its `new` door takes the first segment element, and CBOR/JSON staged reads enter the same TryFrom door so zero elements reject with the min-one RangeCheck. Preserve/canonical retain positional encoding; JSON is a required minItems-one array; wasm and component project the first-element constructor input plus a restricted-list getter. Other bounded windows are separately supported; multiple, same-major/value-discriminator, and fixed/plain-group forms remain graceful rejections. RFC8610 §3.2, §3.4.

A bounded occurrence on a bare-type entry in a HETEROGENEOUS array is an open-array segment with its own inclusive `BoundedVec<T, MIN, MAX>` carrier. It may be final, or a safe middle segment before an immediate mandatory, one-item suffix. A variable middle window needs a field-codec-free, effective, CBOR-major-disjoint boundary: its heads are generator-proven (including mandatory outer framing) or declared by a transparent custom-codec alias with `@custom_wire_major`; an undeclared custom-owned or direct opaque-extern head remains unproven. An exact `N*N` window stops by count and may share the suffix's major or use custom-/extern-owned heads. Native construction takes the complete checked carrier; CBOR and JSON stage loose elements then enter one `TryFrom` door; wasm takes the matching bounded list wrapper; and component takes a fallible `list<T>` conversion. JSON makes the field required and publishes both bounds; preserve/canonical retain positional element encodings. `*0` / `0*0` is the checked exact-zero carrier, while bare `*` / `0*` and `+` / `1*` retain their established Vec and NonEmptyVec APIs. Multiple, variable same-major/value-discriminator, and group/group-choice/plain-group forms remain graceful rejections. RFC8610 §3.2, §3.4.

A zero-or-more occurrence can target a named group reference. RFC 8610 repeats the group's member sequence by flat concatenation; a generator must not substitute a homogeneous collection whose elements each write their own array header. RFC8610 §2.2.1, §3.2.
A zero-or-more occurrence can target a named group reference in map representation; this probes the named-group map occupant rather than an inline table. RFC8610 §2.2.1, §3.2, §3.5.

A zero-or-more occurrence targeting a BARE (unkeyed) fixed value as an array element: `[* 5]` repeats a literal, not a type. The count-permitting side of the fixed-value cardinality boundary; its exactly-once side is `contain.array-element.type2.value.bare_exactly_once` (`[5, x: uint]`) and its keyed count-permitting siblings are `contain.occurrence-target.type2.value.optional_keyed_array` / `.optional_keyed_map`. RFC8610 §3.2, §3.4, §2.1; ABNF grpent = [occur S] type -> type2 value.

An optional occurrence targeting a bare fixed value as an array element: `[? 5]` admits zero or one literal. Same count-permitting side as `contain.occurrence-target.type2.value.zero_array` / `.plus_array`, varying only the marker; the exactly-once side is `contain.array-element.type2.value.bare_exactly_once` and the KEYED optional counterpart is `contain.occurrence-target.type2.value.optional_keyed_array`. RFC8610 §3.2, §3.4, §2.1; ABNF grpent = [occur S] type -> type2 value.

A one-or-more occurrence targeting a bare fixed value as an array element: `[+ 5]` admits one or more repetitions of a literal. Completes the marker sweep over the count-permitting side beside `contain.occurrence-target.type2.value.zero_array` / `.optional_array`; the exactly-once side is `contain.array-element.type2.value.bare_exactly_once`. RFC8610 §3.2, §3.4, §2.1; ABNF grpent = [occur S] type -> type2 value.

The MAP-representation sibling of the bare-fixed-value occurrence rows: a `*` occurrence on a type-domain arrow entry whose VALUE domain is a literal (`{ * uint => 5 }`), so the repeated payload per table entry is a fixed value. The keyed side of the same boundary in map representation is `contain.occurrence-target.type2.value.optional_keyed_map`; the array-representation count-permitting sibling is `.zero_array`. RFC8610 §3.2, §3.5.2, §2.1; ABNF grpent = [occur S] memberkey type -> type2 value.

The KEYED side of the fixed-value cardinality boundary in map representation: an optional occurrence on a member whose key is a bareword and whose value is a literal (`{ ? k: 5, j: uint }`), so the cardinality lives on a named entry rather than on a table row. Its bare/table counterpart is `contain.occurrence-target.type2.value.table_map` (`{ * uint => 5 }`) and its array-representation twin is `.optional_keyed_array`; the same shape appears in `tests/corpus/optional_fixed_member.cddl` (`opt_fixed_map`). Two-field example to match the shape convention of the sibling `role.map-value` rows. RFC8610 §3.2, §3.5.1, §2.1; ABNF grpent = [occur S] memberkey S type.

The KEYED side of the fixed-value cardinality boundary in array representation: an optional occurrence on a LABELLED array member whose type is a literal (`[x: uint, ? v: 5, label: tstr]`). Its bare counterpart is `contain.occurrence-target.type2.value.optional_array` (`[? 5]`) and its map twin is `.optional_keyed_map`. The trailing `label: tstr` is deliberate: an array optional whose CBOR major type overlaps the FOLLOWING field trips the ambiguity guard documented in `tests/corpus/optional_fixed_member.cddl`, so a Text-classed successor to the Uint-classed optional keeps this cell on the fixed-value-under-occurrence axis rather than on the guard. RFC8610 §3.2, §3.4, §2.1; ABNF grpent = [occur S] memberkey S type.

The content of #6.n(...) is any `type`, so a map may be tagged. NOTE: a tag accepts an INLINE anonymous map (supported) — unlike a choice/array/map-value position, which requires the nested composite to be named. RFC8610 §3.6, §3.5. (2-field example by this file's convention, not a workaround: a single-field bareword map is itself supported, pinned by tests/corpus/single_field_map.cddl.)
Tag content is a full `type`, so a `/` type-choice may be tagged directly: `#6.10(int / tstr)`. RFC8610 §3.6, §2.2.2; ABNF tagged-data -> type (type-choice).
`~name` is a type2, so it may be a whole rule body, not only nested inside a composite: `g = ~h`. RFC8610 §3.7; ABNF rule -> type -> type2 unwrap.
The content of #6.n(...) is any `type`, which includes another tag -> #6.x(#6.y(T)) is legal CDDL.

features.desc: Overrides the generated name of a map field, array element, or choice variant (e.g. integer-keyed map fields become readable names).
features.title: @name — explicit field/variant name

features.desc: On a rule in an extern-deps scope (a stub or an extern-interface export), pins the FINAL Rust name the dependency's own codegen version derived, so the consumer reads the name instead of re-deriving it — killing cross-version naming skew. Rejected gracefully on exported rules (the consumer IS the deriving version there); a pin equal to today's derivation changes nothing (plain grouped import), so faithful-stub migration stays byte-identical.
features.title: @rust_name — dependency-pinned Rust type name

features.desc: Attaches a rust doc-comment at field, struct, variant, or rule level (plain alias and @newtype rules). Cannot contain '@'.
features.example:
documented = [
  foo: text, ; @doc a field comment
  bar: uint
] ; @doc struct doc
documented_alias = uint ; @doc an alias rule doc
features.title: @doc — rust doc comment

features.desc: Turns `foo = uint` from a `type Foo = u64` alias into a `struct Foo(u64)` newtype; may name an optional getter.
features.title: @newtype — wrapper struct instead of alias

features.desc: The tolerate-and-drop flavor of an open struct-map rest row (`* k => v` after fixed keys) or an open-array occurrence segment (`* t` final, or a safe middle `* t` before one mandatory major-disjoint suffix). Unknown map entries / repeated array elements are typed-deserialized (for maps, key AND value, so the stream advances past nested containers) and then DROPPED: no `rest` field is emitted, serialize re-emits only the declared members, and JSON/schemars/wasm are a closed struct's. This is the documented-lossy counterpart to the default capture flavor (byte round-trips do not hold for wire data carrying unknown entries / ignored array elements). Valid ONLY on a recognized loose `* k => v` rest row or loose final/safe-middle `* t` segment — every other placement (rule/alias/union/table/whole-array/field, unsafe non-final placement, or restricted window) is a graceful rejection — and rejected together with --preserve-encodings (a preserve crate's byte-exact contract can't hold for a lossy type), with @duplicates (no captured container / no keys for a policy to govern), and with @name (no field to name). The directive is bare and argument-less.
features.title: @ignore — tolerate-and-drop open struct-map row / array segment

features.desc: Skips generating a named alias for the type; uses the underlying type directly at every use site.
features.title: @no_alias — inline the type, emit no alias

features.desc: Forces a type to derive Ord/PartialOrd or Hash even if it isn't used as a map key in the spec (so hand-written utility code can key on it).
features.title: @used_as_key — force Ord/Hash derives

features.desc: Flavor argument narrowing @used_as_key to the hash family: derives only Hash, Eq, PartialEq (so a downstream HashMap key compiles), mode-independent unlike the bare tag's full mode-dependent bundle. Propagates transitively to contained types.
features.title: @used_as_key hash — narrowed Hash derive family

features.desc: Flavor argument narrowing @used_as_key to the ord family: derives only Ord, PartialOrd, Eq, PartialEq (so a downstream BTreeMap key compiles), mode-independent unlike the bare tag's full mode-dependent bundle. Propagates transitively to contained types.
features.title: @used_as_key ord — narrowed Ord derive family

features.desc: Flavor argument combining both narrowed families: derives the union Hash, Ord, PartialOrd, Eq, PartialEq, mode-independent unlike the bare tag whose Hash is mode-dependent. Order of the two words is irrelevant. Propagates transitively to contained types.
features.example: keyed = [a: uint, b: text] ; @used_as_key hash ord
features.title: @used_as_key hash ord — union of the hash and ord families

features.desc: Forces minting the loose-list wasm wrapper (FooList = [* foo] equivalent) for the tagged type even when the spec never contains that list inline, so this crate canonically hosts the wrapper class (and satisfies downstream --wrapper-requests consumers asking for that shape).
features.title: @used_as_elem — mint the canonical loose-list wasm wrapper

features.desc: On a _CDDL_CODEGEN_EXTERN_TYPE_ generic, makes instances whose argument is a _CDDL_CODEGEN_RAW_BYTES_TYPE_ alias the user-owned <ExternName>RawBytes wrapper flavor instead of the plain name (one wrapper type cannot serve both trait-bound and raw-bytes elements — the blanket impls would conflict). Opt-in only, so a wrapper bound solely on RawBytesEncoding keeps compiling under the plain name.
features.title: @raw_bytes_flavor — extern generic raw-bytes wrapper flavor

features.desc: On a _CDDL_CODEGEN_EXTERN_TYPE_ or _CDDL_CODEGEN_RAW_BYTES_TYPE_ rule, declares that the externally-defined rust type derives Copy, so the generator stops emitting a defensive .clone() at boundaries that move the value (map-key deserialize loops, wasm getters/accessors). The declaring crate emits a compile-time Copy assertion for the type, so a false @copy fails that crate's own build. Rides the extern-interface seam like @raw_bytes_flavor, so --extern-import consumers inherit it. The wasm face (a distinct wrapper) is not Copy, so the wasm->rust boundary keeps its clone.
features.title: @copy — extern/raw-bytes type derives Copy, drop boundary clones

features.desc: Per-rule duplicates policy, reject flavor: on a set/array collection rule ([* a] / [+ a], including the tag-258 set idiom) the transparent alias swaps to the order-preserving uniqueness twin OrderedSet/NonEmptyOrderedSet, whose single TryFrom door refuses a duplicate (DeserializeFailure::DuplicateKey) identically on the wire and through the API. Accepted (duplicate-free) input still re-emits byte-exactly — rejection narrows the accepted set, never the accepted bytes. On a table, reject is the default (writing it is an accepted self-documenting no-op). The directive takes exactly one required argument; there is no bare form (a missing/unknown argument is a parse-time panic).
features.title: @duplicates reject — duplicate-free set/array collections

features.desc: Per-rule duplicates policy, preserve flavor: on a table rule ({* k => v}, {+ k => v}, or a bounded homogeneous window) the transparent alias swaps to the Vec<(K, V)>-backed PairMap/NonEmptyPairMap/BoundedPairMap twin — the only shape faithful to both entry order and duplicate keys. BoundedPairMap's single TryFrom door enforces its inclusive entry-count window, so a duplicate-keyed map decodes AND re-emits byte-exactly within the allowed range (driver: pre-Conway Cardano transaction_metadata, whose auxiliary-data hash is computed over the original bytes). JSON diverges to an array of [k, v] pairs (an object would collapse duplicates); under --canonical-form entries stable-sort by encoded key bytes with duplicates adjacent. On a set/array, preserve is the default (writing it is an accepted self-documenting no-op).
features.title: @duplicates preserve — duplicate-preserving pair-map tables

features.desc: Avoids generating/deriving JSON-related traits, on the assumption the user supplies their own.
features.title: @custom_json — suppress generated JSON traits

features.desc: Declares that a rule's rust type is not part of the published JSON-schema surface: under --json-schema-export the json-gen crate's `add_schemas` emits no registration row for it, so it is not one of the crate's declared schema roots. Deliberately narrow — the serde/schemars DERIVES stay (a parent embedding the type still needs them, and the type still appears in the crate's `$defs` whenever a published type references it — the row is the ROOT declaration, not the definition; dropping the derives is the orthogonal, legally combinable @custom_json), and CBOR/wasm/extern-interface output is untouched. Inert when --json-schema-export is off, so one spec generates unedited under several flag sets. Valid on any rule that registers a rust type; on one that registers none (a transparent alias, a generic DEFINITION — only its instantiations are types) there is no row to suppress and generation is rejected by name rather than silently dead.
features.title: @no_json_schema_export — not a published JSON-schema root

features.desc: Replaces generated serialization with a named user function (type-level or field-level).
features.example:
cb = bytes ; @custom_serialize my_ser @custom_deserialize my_deser
holder = [f: cb]
features.title: @custom_serialize — override serialization

features.desc: Replaces generated deserialization with a named user function (type-level or field-level).
features.example:
cb = bytes ; @custom_serialize my_ser @custom_deserialize my_deser
holder = [f: cb]
features.title: @custom_deserialize — override deserialization

features.desc: Beside a complete @custom_serialize/@custom_deserialize pair, declares the codec-visible encoding variables of the wire THAT CODEC writes and reads, so the preserve-encodings signature and the *Encoding sidecar slots follow the declaration instead of the REPLACED type's inferred demand. A comma-separated list (no whitespace) over sz (Option<cbor_event::Sz>), str (StringEncoding) and len (LenEncoding), positional — serialize takes them as trailing arguments in declared order, deserialize returns (value, declared…) — or the keyword none, the explicit empty list for a wire with no framing. Without it, a pair over a SELF-CARRYING type (an extern, a record, bool, any) infers no variables at all and the custom wire's framing is recorded nowhere, so the round trip silently normalizes it; under --preserve-encodings that undeclared spelling is now a graceful rejection. Requires BOTH halves in the same position (rule or field) and binds to the pair beside it, so a field-level pair never inherits a shadowed alias's declaration. Inert without --preserve-encodings. Aggregate (per-element Vec/BTreeMap) and tag-presence encodings are deliberately not declarable.
features.example:
cb = bytes ; @custom_serialize my_ser @custom_deserialize my_deser @custom_encodings sz,str
holder = [f: cb]
features.rfc: cddl-codegen comment DSL; docs/docs/comment_dsl.mdx §@custom_serialize / @custom_deserialize (Declaring the wire's encoding variables); src/comment_ast.rs
features.title: @custom_encodings — the custom codec declares its own wire's encoding variables

features.desc: The second member of the wire-facts declaration family beside @custom_encodings. Written beside a complete @custom_serialize/@custom_deserialize pair, declares which of the eight CBOR major types the wire THAT CODEC writes begins with, as exactly one of uint / nint / bytes / text / array / map / tag / simple (an unknown token is a loud parse failure naming the set). Its consumers are an open table's typed row (t = { * K_t => V_t, * K_r => V_r }) and either boundary of a variable middle open array (m = [prefix, * elem, suffix]). The table dispatch must peek the declared major before any key deserializer runs; middle validation needs both effective boundary majors, and the emitted greedy loop peeks the repeated side only before the ordinary suffix reader runs. There the generator's own cbor_types() answers about the type the codec REPLACED, so a codec writing hex TEXT over a raw-bytes marker would dispatch major 2 and never match its own keys. REQUIRED when either reader must see the codec-owned head (its absence is a graceful rejection naming the directive); mandatory generated outer tag/.cbor framing supplies its own head and does not consume the declaration. A graceful rejection where nothing consumes it, where the pair is incomplete or absent, and on a rule that mints a struct (the declaration is read through the rule's transparent alias entry, which a struct-minting rule has none of). Final/exact middle placements and optional-prefix lookahead do not consume it; field-local declarations remain refused. Consumed somewhere is enough, so one alias may key an open table, prove a middle boundary, AND appear at a field. Unlike @custom_encodings it is not gated on --preserve-encodings.
features.rfc: cddl-codegen comment DSL; docs/docs/comment_dsl.mdx §Declaring the wire's major type (@custom_wire_major); src/comment_ast.rs
features.title: @custom_wire_major — the custom codec declares which CBOR major type its wire starts with

features.desc: On a LOCALLY-declared, non-generic _CDDL_CODEGEN_EXTERN_TYPE_ or _CDDL_CODEGEN_RAW_BYTES_TYPE_ rule, declares that the named STRUCTURAL wasm companion classes of that type (its <Name>List, Map<Name>To…, …) already exist in a sibling wasm crate: the generator emits `use <path>::<Class>;` and mints no local #[wasm_bindgen] class of that name, so both crates can link into one cdylib without a duplicate __wbg_<class>_free symbol. Both markers qualify because both name a type this crate does not define while the generator still mints that type's companions under its ident. Argument is `<use_path_prefix>=<Class>[,<Class>…]`, whitespace-free; only LISTED classes defer, so an unlisted companion of the same type still mints locally. The dependency-keyed --extern-wrapper-index / --workspace-dep cannot serve this case (both key on a constituent's owning DEPENDENCY, and a local marker has no dep edge; an index also lists only what generation minted, never a hand-written class), so a dep-scoped rule carrying it is rejected naming those flags. Inert without --wasm.
features.title: @extern_companions — reference a sibling crate's wasm companion classes

features.desc: Treats the rule as an externally-defined type implementing Serialize/Deserialize; no code is generated for it. (ruby/rust reject the undefined typename — expected for a vendor extension.)
features.title: _CDDL_CODEGEN_EXTERN_TYPE_ — compose in a hand-written type

features.desc: Encodes as bytes but defers to an external type implementing the RawBytesEncoding trait. (ruby/rust reject the undefined typename — expected.)
features.title: _CDDL_CODEGEN_RAW_BYTES_TYPE_ — bytes with hand-written constraints

features.desc: A generic extern base the spec never instantiates. Nothing is emitted for it beyond the re-export glue naming the bare base (`pub use crate::<Base>;`) in both faces: it names no concrete type, so the extern-interface self-check and the json-gen schema registrar must both SKIP it — a row spelling a bare `<Base>` would be E0107 against the parameterized type the marker declares.
features.title: _CDDL_CODEGEN_EXTERN_TYPE_ generic base with NO instances — re-export only

features.desc: A generic extern base the spec binds (`ext_gen<uint>`). The rust crate aliases the instance itself (`pub type ExtGenU64 = ExtGen<u64>;`) and re-exports only the BASE, so one hand-written generic definition serves every instance; the wasm crate, which has no generics, instead requires a user-provided concrete `ExtGenU64` wrapper and re-exports THAT name.
features.title: _CDDL_CODEGEN_EXTERN_TYPE_ generic base WITH an instance — per-instance alias

features.desc: The raw-bytes marker's answer to the same generic-base axis the two extern rows above enumerate, and the opposite one: an extern base may legitimately be parameterized (it is an arbitrary hand-written type), but a raw-bytes type IS its own bytes and carries no element type for a parameter to name, so a generic base is refused by name at parse time rather than generating self-check and schema rows spelling a bare base that cannot compile against the parameterized type the marker declares. The remedy the message names is to declare it non-generic. Refused with and without instances, under --wasm=true and --wasm=false alike.
features.title: _CDDL_CODEGEN_RAW_BYTES_TYPE_ generic base — refused at parse time

features.desc: Alternation between whole groups: the group matches one of several grpchoice branches.
features.title: Group choice (//)

features.desc: A grpchoice is a sequence of group entries separated by optional commas (optcom = S ["," S]).
features.title: Group-entry sequence

features.desc: A group entry that is a type, optionally preceded by a memberkey (named member) and/or an occurrence indicator; with the memberkey ABSENT it is a positional, type-only element. This example isolates the absent-memberkey path (the memberkey-present path is covered by memberkey.*).
features.title: Member entry (optional occur + optional memberkey + type)

features.desc: A group entry that references a named group by name, inlining that group's entries; may carry generic args and an occurrence.
features.title: Group-name reference entry

features.desc: A group entry that is itself a parenthesized group; the isolated form is just `(...)` as one entry (an occurrence can then apply to the whole sub-group — see occurrence-target containment).
features.title: Inline (parenthesized) group entry

features.desc: A memberkey given as a full type expression followed by =>; the key matches any data item of that type (table / general form).
features.title: Type memberkey (t =>)

features.desc: A memberkey given as a bareword (id) followed by ':'; shorthand for the text-string key "k" => and carries an implicit cut.
features.title: Bareword memberkey (k:)

features.desc: A memberkey given as a literal value (number/text/bytes) followed by ':'; equivalent to value => and carries an implicit cut.
features.title: Value memberkey (1:)

features.desc: The optional '^' marks a => memberkey as a cut, so a matched key is not also offered to later (e.g. wildcard) entries; the ':' shortcut forms (bareword/value) carry this cut implicitly.
features.title: Cut in a => memberkey (^)

features.desc: The entry occurs zero or one time.
features.title: Optional occurrence (?)

features.desc: Bare '*' with both bounds omitted: the entry occurs any number of times, including zero.
features.title: Zero-or-more occurrence (*)

features.desc: The entry occurs one or more times (equivalent to 1*).
features.title: One-or-more occurrence (+)

features.desc: Same '*' production as zero-or-more but with explicit lower and/or upper bound (n*, *m, or n*m): the entry occurs between n and m times.
features.title: Bounded occurrence (n*m)

features.desc: One-sided variation of occur.bounded: a lower-bound-only occurrence (`2*`) whose count check has NO upper arm — the entry occurs at least n times, unbounded above. A distinct enforcement surface from the two-sided `2*5` base row, per the "Intra-alternative variation rows" lesson that the enforcement axis reaches only as far as row enumeration.
features.title: Lower-bound-only occurrence (n*)

features.desc: One-sided variation of occur.bounded: an upper-bound-only, zero-permitting occurrence (`*5`) — the entry occurs at most m times, zero allowed. On the ARRAY side this is a type-enforced `BoundedVec<T, 0, m>` length window. A lone homogeneous unique-key table with the same window is likewise a `BoundedMap`; the distinct unsupported map-side context is a zero-permitting keyed struct-map field, which remains rejected rather than narrowed.
